questions.prompt:
What exact output does code example 1 in this lesson produce?

point = (3, 4)
unique = {1, 2, 2, 3}
print('Point tuple:', point, 'set contains', sorted(unique))
print(sorted({1, 2} & {2, 3}))
questions.explanation:
LINE-BY-LINE WALKTHROUGH
`point = (3, 4)` — Binds the evaluated expression to a name; without the assignment, later lines cannot reuse that result.
`unique = {1, 2, 2, 3}` — Binds the evaluated expression to a name; without the assignment, later lines cannot reuse that result.
`print('Point tuple:', point, 'set contains', sorted(unique))` — Runs an expression; print displays a value and calls may have side effects—without the line, that action does not occur.
`print(sorted({1, 2} & {2, 3}))` — Runs an expression; print displays a value and calls may have side effects—without the line, that action does not occur.

A comprehension transforms and filters data in one expression; a regular loop can be clearer when logic grows.
